title: Tensor-product Mittag-Leffler condition gives Mittag-Leffler Hom systems
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, and $(M_i,f_{ij})_{i\in I}$ a directed system of finitely presented $R$-modules. A module is finitely presented here if it is the cokernel of an $R$-linear map $R^a\to R^b$ for finite integers $a,b\ge0$. Let the compatible maps $M_i\to M$ exhibit an $R$-module $M$ as its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose $M$ is Mittag-Leffler in the tensor-product sense [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module]. Then for every $R$-module $N$ and every $i\in I$ there is $j\ge i$ such that for every $k\ge j$ the images of the precomposition maps $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_k,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,N)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_j,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,N)$ are equal. No countability of $I$ or finite-generation assumption on $N$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), (2) implies (1), followed by Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), condition (4).

proof.text: Fix $i\in I$ and write $u_s:M_s\to M$ for the colimit maps. Apply [lem-trf-universal-tensor-kernel-witness] to $P=M_i$, $f=u_i$ and the tensor-product Mittag-Leffler module $M$. The source $M_i$ is finitely presented by hypothesis. Obtain a set-sized $R$-module $T$ and $z\in M_i\otimes_RT$ with $(u_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)(z)=0$, such that each $x\in\ker(u_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)$ for finitely presented $Q$ equals $(\mathrm{id}_{M_i}\otimes q)(z)$ for some $R$-linear $q:T\to Q$.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), proof of (2) implies (1): finite-presentation representatives, product of all kernel pairs, and the first commutative square; tensor-product input Tag 059K (proposition-fp-tensor).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-tensor-witness-eventual-factorization] to the given small nonempty directed system, its colimit cocone, the index $i$, and the $T,z$ from step 1. Both the vanishing and the universal evaluation hypothesis are precisely the conclusions of step 1, and every stage is finitely presented. Obtain one $j\ge i$ such that for every $k\ge j$ some $R$-linear $h_k:M_k\to M_j$ satisfies $f_{ij}=h_k\circ f_{ik}$. The same $j$ will work for every target module $N$.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), proof of (2) implies (1), death of the product-kernel element, implemented directly in the given colimit as in Tag 059L (lemma-kernel-tensored-fp); Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), proof of (2) implies (3), using Tag 059D (lemma-domination) and Tag 059C (lemma-domination-fp).

proof.text: Let $N$ be any $R$-module and $k\ge j$. An element of the image of $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_j,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,N)$ has the form $a\circ f_{ij}$ for $a:M_j\to N$. Step 2 rewrites it as $(a\circ h_k)\circ f_{ik}$, so it is in the image from $M_k$. Conversely, if $b:M_k\to N$, then $b\circ f_{ik}=(b\circ f_{jk})\circ f_{ij}$ by the directed-system identity $f_{ik}=f_{jk}\circ f_{ij}$. Thus the two images are equal for every $k\ge j$. This proves the required assertion for all $i$ and $N$, without countability or any finiteness condition on $N$.

source.place: Tag 059E, proposition-ML-characterization, (3) implies (4); both image inclusions written explicitly.

proof_origin.place: Tag 059M, proposition-ML-tensor, (2) implies (1), and Tag 059E, proposition-ML-characterization, (2) implies (3) implies (4). The universal kernel element is killed in the given system directly, as in Tag 059L.
